videos.script: The last lesson asks where the clinic's data lives, and who can reach it there. {{three}} Three words get mixed up. Residency is where the data is. Sovereignty is whose law can reach it. Compliance is whether you follow the rules, and can prove it. {{lgpd}} Brazil's LGPD allows data to leave the country only on certain grounds. In a cloud, leaving takes one setting. {{loop}} So you will find every copy, with a loop and a tag. One bucket of patient data turns up in Virginia. {{none}} And its region prints as None. That is the trap: the copy abroad reads as nothing. {{guardrail}} Then you write a guardrail that keeps new copies in São Paulo. Your lab stores it and cannot enforce it, and you will see exactly why that matters. {{law}} Last, the laws that follow the provider rather than the data, and what to show an auditor. {{end}}
